children.text: Building on this legacy, the Umm Al Quwain campus was inaugurated in September 2014 with an initial cohort of 200 students from Kindergarten through Grade 7. In 10 years, the UAQ campus has flourished to serve approximately 1,425 learners from KG1 to Grade 12, of whom 86% are Emiratis, 10% are other Arab expatriates, and 4% hail from non-Arab backgrounds such as Russia and Canada.

Today, SAIS - UAQ, under the leadership of Ms. Carole Sarkis Abboud, serves four different phases - Kindergarten, Elementary, Middle School, and High School. Our multicultural faculty represents over ten nationalities, including educators from Canada, the United States, New Zealand, South Africa, Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Egypt, Romania, and Armenia. The campus itself features 59 classrooms, four staff rooms, a Head of Department office, dedicated art and computer labs, four science laboratories, a library, gymnasium, canteens, prayer rooms, multiple playgrounds and swimming pools, a bookstore, and a full suite of administrative and support facilities.

heading.title: Sharjah American International School (SAIS) first opened its doors in Sharjah in 1997 under the vision of Dr. Aisha Al Sayyar and Dr. Nawaf Fawaz.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ reception lobby

children.text: Our curriculum is guided by the AERO (American Education Reaches Out) standards, which provide a clear and consistent framework across all subjects and grade levels. These standards help our teachers design thoughtful, engaging lessons that build essential knowledge and skills.

Using AERO, we ensure that students are not only meeting academic benchmarks but also developing critical thinking, creativity, and real-world problem-solving abilities. Lessons are flexible and student-centered, allowing teachers to adapt instruction based on individual strengths, interests, and learning styles.

In addition to core subjects, students can choose from a wide variety of elective and AP courses to deepen our learner's knowledge and ensure their college readiness. Whether through core classes, electives, or AP courses, our goal is to prepare students to thrive in school and in the world ahead.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ teacher guiding two students in class

children.text: Our staff communicate with stakeholders through various channels to ensure students' well-being and academic success. Teachers create an inclusive environment by planning lessons that meet the needs of all learners, including students of determination and those who are gifted and talented. Student-led national and international events are regularly held at the school, helping students stay actively engaged with the wider community.

At SAIS - UAQ, we are committed to preparing our students to become lifelong learners who are curious, resilient, and driven to grow. We focus on developing strong character values such as integrity, respect, and responsibility. Through academic and personal development, we encourage our students to contribute positively to their community and make a meaningful difference in the world around them.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ students playing maracas in music class

children.text: “Develop a passion for learning. If you do, you will never cease to grow.”
Anthony J. D’Angelo

Today, the role of a school is not only to pursue academic excellence but also to motivate and empower its students to be lifelong learners, critical thinkers, and productive members of an ever-changing global society.

At Sharjah American International School, we foster a productive learning environment that accommodates students’ unique needs and empower them to thrive for excellence. This can only be possible in a holistic, student-centered environment, where teachers as facilitators of learning differentiate instruction to support diverse learning styles, identify and nurture individual talents, skills, and abilities of students, and encourage them to achieve their full potential. Teachers provide students with a platform to think critically, express, and exhibit their knowledge and skills, and positively contribute to the community.

We strongly believe in the importance of teachers, parents, and administrators collaborating and communicating openly and frequently to improve students’ performance and well-being. The consistent support of the parents has empowered us to do more and more. I pay my gratitude to them for their trust in us.
I am confident that all our students are equipped with the essential skills to face future challenges with confidence and are poised to make a meaningful impact on tomorrow’s society.

Please enjoy exploring our website. You will find important and relevant information about our school. We will also be delighted to welcome you for a tour of our spacious classrooms and extensive facilities.
Carole Sarkis Abboud

children.text: Our Middle School program supports students through the important transition toward High School education. Middle School students experience a subject-based learning environment that encourages academic growth, independence, critical thinking, and personal responsibility.

The learning environment is designed to meet the developmental needs of middle school learners while providing a safe, supportive, and engaging atmosphere. Through a balanced academic program, dedicated teachers, and a strong sense of community, students are encouraged to build confidence, develop their skills, and prepare successfully for high school and beyond.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ middle school students reading in the library

children.text: Transitions are carefully considered in the design of teaching and learning approaches. Teachers utilize a variety of instructional strategies tailored to students’ developmental stages and subject areas, fostering independence, critical thinking, creativity, and collaboration.

The curriculum is structured to provide a balanced blend of academic rigor, inquiry-based learning, and opportunities for exploration and self-discovery, ensuring that students thrive academically, socially, and emotionally throughout their educational journey.

heading.title: Tailored Instruction  for Every Stage of Learning

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ middle school student playing keyboard during music class

children.text: The Middle School curriculums designed to deepen students’ subject knowledge while continuing to develop critical thinking, creativity, communication, and independent learning skills.
Students engage in a balanced academic program that includes core subjects, specialist instruction, electives, and enrichment opportunities that support both academic and personal growth.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ students participating in class

children.text: In Middle School, assessment becomes more structured while continuing to focus on student development and continuous improvement. Students are assessed through quizzes, unit tests, formative assessments, projects, performance tasks, presentations, classwork, and project-based assessments.

Assessment practices are designed to measure students’ understanding, application of knowledge, analytical thinking, and ability to communicate their learning effectively. Teachers use assessment data to identify students’ strengths, address learning gaps, and provide targeted support when needed.

image.alt: SAIS - UAQ middle school students reviewing a book together

children.text: Middle School students also complete more formal assessments, including semester-based tests and final examinations where applicable. These assessments help prepare students for the academic expectations of High School.

In addition, students receive regular preparation for external assessments through skill-based practice, data-informed instruction, and exposure to international assessment-style questions that develop reasoning, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills.

children.text: We consider every application fairly and in accordance with the requirements of the United Arab Emirates Ministry of Education (MOE). Each application is reviewed based on academic records, placement assessment results, and seat availability in the requested grade level.

SAIS - UAQ reserves the right to deny or withdraw an offer of enrollment if a student continues to demonstrate significant behavioral concerns despite the school’s support and intervention measures, in accordance with MOE guidelines. Such decisions are made to ensure that all students can thrive in a safe, respectful, and productive learning environment.
